CSCA Syllabus

Open the official subject outlines, see what each paper covers, and confirm which ones your university requires.

What does the CSCA syllabus cover?

The official CSCA syllabus has separate outlines for Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and two Professional Chinese tracks. Open the organizer's PDFs below to check the full scope of each paper. The linked 2025 outlines list four Mathematics modules, five Physics modules and four Chemistry modules, summarised here for easier study.

CSCA.ai offers practice for Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, but not Professional Chinese. Always check the current official CSCA syllabi before building your plan. The PDF links below open on the official CSCA website; the CSCA.ai topic guides are independent study summaries. Source links and topic summary last checked 25 October 2026.

Explore the three subject outlines

The official Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry papers each contain 48 single-choice questions, last 60 minutes and may be taken in Chinese or English. The topic guides below explain what to study; use the official outline for the full scope.

Mathematics

48 questions · 60 minutes

Sets and inequalities

Set operations, representations, and methods for solving quadratic and rational inequalities.

Functions and sequences

Function properties, elementary functions, arithmetic and geometric sequences, and basic derivatives.

Geometry and algebra

Lines and conics, vectors, complex numbers, coordinate geometry, and simple solid geometry.

Probability and statistics

Classical probability, data measures such as mean and variance, and basic normal distribution ideas.

Read Mathematics syllabus guide Explore Mathematics Official Mathematics syllabus (PDF)

Physics

48 questions · 60 minutes

Mechanics

Motion, forces, work, energy, momentum, circular motion, and gravitation.

Electromagnetism

Electric fields, direct-current circuits, magnetic fields, and electromagnetic induction.

Thermodynamics

Molecular motion, ideal gases, heat, and the first law of thermodynamics.

Optics

Reflection, refraction, interference, and diffraction of light.

Modern physics

The photoelectric effect, atomic structure, and nuclear physics.

Read Physics syllabus guide Explore Physics Official Physics syllabus (PDF)

Chemistry

48 questions · 60 minutes

Core concepts and calculations

Chemical symbols, equations, amount of substance, molar mass, gases, solutions, and stoichiometry.

Properties and reactions

Common inorganic substances, acids, bases, salts, hydrocarbons, redox reactions, and ionic reactions.

Chemical theories and laws

Atomic structure, periodic law, bonding, reaction rate, equilibrium, and electrolyte solutions.

Experiments and applications

Laboratory safety, gas preparation, separation and purification, testing methods, and industrial processes.

Read Chemistry syllabus guide Explore Chemistry Official Chemistry syllabus (PDF)

Where is the Professional Chinese syllabus?

The organizer publishes separate outlines for Chinese for Humanities (文科中文) and Chinese for Science (理科中文). Each paper has 80 single-choice questions in 90 minutes, in Chinese. Your university and application route determine whether you need this paper and which track to take. CSCA.ai does not currently offer practice for either track.

Understand the two tracks Official Humanities outline (PDF)Official Science outline (PDF)

Which CSCA papers do I need?

Your application route, university and programme determine the papers to register for. The official CSCA exam introduction lists Mathematics among the required papers for the undergraduate application routes it describes. Physics and Chemistry depend on the programme; Professional Chinese requirements also depend on the application route and language of instruction. Check your university notice before booking.
Read the official exam introduction 

How should I use the syllabus to study?

Step 1
Confirm your papers

Read your intended university and programme notice before choosing subjects or an exam language.

Step 2
Read the official outline

Use the current CSCA syllabus for each paper as the final topic checklist. This overview is a study aid.

Step 3
Practise and review

Try questions by subject, review the reasoning, and spend your next session on the topics you missed.

Turn the syllabus into a study plan.

Try focused questions in a subject, review your answers, and choose the next topic to study.
